answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 48x32 rectangle. Rows 0-6 are a pale snow terrace, closed by a dark line at row 6. Rows 7-31 are a brownish ramp seen from above, crossed by thin bluish step lines at rows 10, 14, 19, 23 and 27. Dark vertical strips on the left and right edges are the cut walls seen edge-on. No vertical south face of 3 or more rows is drawn. The step lines read as flat grade breaks on a surface seen from above, not as a front face. Rows 29-31 get lighter toward the bottom edge, which reads as snow on the lower terrace. As a terrain tile this is a plan-view ramp, not a standing object with a top and a front.

styleAnswer.evidence: By eye the candidate is a pale pink-grey slab crossed by a few thin horizontal blue-grey lines for the ramp steps. Between the lines the surface is nearly uniform, with no snow grain, speckle, per-step highlight or shaded clumps. Only about 3 real lightness steps carry the material, and the raw palette is just 9 colours. The measured 6 visible tones per tile roughly matches the paving reference (7) and beats the grass (3), but the extra tones come from the line colours, not from shading inside the material. The measured 0% near-flat coverage looks generous against the picture, which shows broad quiet fills. The edges are tinted rather than neutral black, but there is no real material-tone outline. Overall it reads thinner and flatter than the grass and paving references, which have grain, tufts and stone-by-stone shading. That makes it a flat, sticker-like stripe pattern, so it fails.
